newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS - Paris stocks hit record, boosted by polls.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Paris stocks hit record, boosted by polls.

text.p: European stocks made some healthy gains on Wednesday and the Paris bourse surged to an all-time high on the back of fresh opinion polls showing a big win for the centre-right government in opcoming elections.

In currencies, the dollar strengthened against the mark, bolstered by supportive comments from a Bundesbank council member and rekindled speculation that the U.S. central bank may increase interest rates next week.

London and Frankfurt, which closed at record levels on Tuesday, made a mixed start. French shares, however, made the best running, hitting an intra-day record of 2765.91 points on the CAC 40 index and eclipsing the previous all-time high of 2,736.71 set two months ago.

Investors in most European capitals were also cheered by the stronger dollar which improved export prospects but Paris was given the added lift of a poll lead for the government parties, regarded as more sympathetic to business.
"All signs are on green, the dollar, the bond market and the polls," a broker said.

A CSA poll on Tuesday night gave 317 seats to the centre-right majority against 215 to the Socialists and allies. This followed a BVA poll giving 303 to the majority and 226 to the Socialists and allies.
Jacques Chahine Finance has predicted that if the government parties win, fund managers saw the CAC heading above 3,000. If the Socialists win it could fall to 2,400.
But dealers said some factors could puncture the French euphoria.

Large fund inflows were currently fuelling the market as foreign funds take comfort from the polls and invest in France, which has been lagging behind other markets. But a poll showing a swing back to the Socialists could scare these investors away again.
In London, Europe's biggest bourse, chalked up gains of 0.5 percent at the start , after a record-breaking run which has seen the blue-chip FTSE 100 index climb 10 percent in the last four weeks.
Stocks eased back slightly by midmorning and dealers said some consolidation was inevitable.
"We won't see much selling pressure today. Very few people want to sell stock at the moment," one senior dealer said. "But market makers will mark down prices until the buyers step in again."
In Frankfurt, trading on the computerised IBIS index climbed 0.6 percent in early dealings but floor trade, which closed at a peak on Tuesday looked decidedly lacklustre, slipping 0.39 per cent .
Deutsche Telekom was a one of the main losers, following reports that Bonn might consider selling some its Telekom shares to help pare back its budget deficit.
On currency markets, the dollar edged higher on the mark after remarks by Bundesbank council member Ernst Welteke that a dollar/mark rate about 1.70 was supported by economic fundamentals.

Traders said the comments from Welteke supported overnight dollar gains against the mark and combined with rekindled talk that the U.S. Federal Reserve may move to lift interest rates again at its policy-making meeting next week.
Speaking at a conference in Vienna, Welteke said "It seems that a dollar rate at around 1.70 marks conforms with the real data."
"Welteke is certainly giving the impression the weakness of the mark is not a problem at these levels," said Nick Stamenkovic, economist at DKB International.

Sources close to the Federal Reserve central bank told Reuters that there was a good chance of a 25 basis point rise in the 5.50 percent Federal funds target rate when the policy-making Federal Open Market
Elsewhere, sterling rallied in early trading against a generally weaker mark . It was at 2.7822 marks compared to 2.7687 in late trade yesterday.

The pound was stronger on Tuesday affter the Bank of England said the recent strength of sterling improved the inflation outlook this year but that another interest rate rise was likely to be necessary to keep a lid on prices.
STOCK PRICES AT 1000 GMT
London's FTSE 100 was up 14.5 points at 4,705.5.
The Paris CAC-40 index was up 44.36 points at 2,763.94.
Frankfurt's DAX index was down 16.06 points at 3,579.09.
CURRENCIES AT 1000 GMT
The dollar stood at 1.7048 marks compared with 1.6965 late in Europe on Tuesday and 118.63 yen versus 118.83.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold was fixed at $349.00 an ounce after closing at $348.05 in London on Tuesday. Silver was up one cent at $4.86.
